evidence.claim: The corridor was part of the Pend O’Reille Highway, a state road established in 1923 to connect Spokane with the border.
evidence.quote: In 1923, a system of roads to connect cities throughout Washington was established. One of the roads, State Road 6, followed a route from Spokane to the Canada–US border. The road was named the Pend O'Reille Highway

evidence.claim: The number’s southern reach shortened in 1973, when SR 20 extended to Newport and took over the stretch south of Tiger.

evidence.claim: In 1942, the FBI arrested George Kubota, Sr., a member of the Japanese-American family that ran a hardware store in Metaline Falls, and imprisoned him in Spokane.
evidence.quote: George Kubota, Sr., the patriarch of a Japanese-American family who ran a hardware store in town, was arrested and imprisoned by the FBI in Spokane.

evidence.claim: The local newspaper’s editors and most town residents protested his arrest and vouched for the family’s loyalty.
evidence.quote: The editors of the Metaline Falls newspaper and the majority of residents in town protested the arrest, vouching for the Kubota family's loyalty.

evidence.claim: The FBI eventually released him, and the family was not sent to an internment camp.
evidence.quote: The FBI eventually released Kubota from custody and did not send the family to an internment camp.
